title: LLM KPI adaptive ingest orchestrator: OTLP/Prometheus bridge with per-model sampling
creator: Samantha Liu
description: Build an adaptive ingest orchestrator that reliably bridges Prometheus-style scraping and OpenTelemetry push models for per-request inference KPIs. The orchestrator will handle tenant-aware routing, model-aware sampling policies, backpressure to edge/ingest tiers, and a small in-flight reservoir aggregator for tail-latency histograms. Goal: reduce cardinality and cost while preserving SLO-aligned signals (p50/p90/p99 latency, error counts by model-version and route, token counts, cache hit rates).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Sidecar + gateway integration can export enriched OTLP spans/metrics with per-request labels (model, route, tenant, kv_prefix_hit) within 250ms overhead in 99th% of local microbench tests. 2) Configurable sampling policies based on model, route, and customer tier apply and are enforced at ingest gateway. 3) Reservoir aggregator produces stable p99 estimates with <5% error vs full histograms on representative traffic. 4) Backpressure path gracefully drops low-priority samples and surfaces alerts to ops with debug traces. 5) Feature rolled out to 10% of traffic behind runtime flag with no increase in error budget.
implementation_notes: - Will introduce a lightweight orchestrator service (k8s deployment) that accepts OTLP/gRPC from sidecars and scrapers. - Orchestrator exposes per-tenant queues and applies sampling rules from a centralized policy store (Redis/etcd). - Reservoir-based tail aggregator runs in-memory with bounded memory; periodically emits downsampled histograms to Prometheus remote_write and OTLP exporters. - Backpressure signalled via gRPC flow control and an HTTP status + Retry-After for scrapers; sidecars fall back to local scratch buffering. - Metrics emitted: ingest_queue_depth, drop_rate_by_policy, reservoir_p99_estimate, per_model_sample_rate, otlp_forward_latency.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): unit/integration tests, local performance benchmark. Phase 2 (staging): run on staging with synthetic mixed-tenancy traffic and compare full ingestion vs sampled pipeline. Phase 3 (canary): enable for 10% production traffic for low-risk tenants; monitor drop_rate, token-billing divergence, and SLO signals. Phase 4: progressive ramp, allow opt-out for customers with high-fidelity requirements. Feature flag + kill switch baked into gateway.
monitoring_and_alerts: Create dashboards for ingest_queue_depth, drop_rate_by_policy, reservoir_error_ratio, otlp_forward_latency, sidecar_export_errors. Add alerts: reservoir_error_ratio > 0.1 for 5m, enqueue_delay_p50 > 500ms, drop_rate_by_policy > 0.05 for 5m. Add runbook entries for debug steps and emergency disablement.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for sampling rules and policy evaluation. 2) Integration tests: sidecar -> orchestrator -> remote_write. 3) Load tests with representative request shapes (short chat turns, long generations, embeddings) to verify memory and latency. 4) A/B comparison in staging comparing p99 estimates to full-histogram baseline. 5) Chaos tests: simulate upstream OTLP spikes and broker failures to validate backpressure and safe degradation.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: full-fidelity histograms are expensive; reservoir aggregation adds bounded error but enables 10-20x ingestion cost reductions. Chose reservoir approach over sketching to preserve interpretability for p99. Policy evaluation moved out of the hot path by caching decisions for 30s. Consideration: customers who require exact billing accuracy will be able to opt into high-fidelity route.
